2. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed the aforesaid Suit for a declaration that the order dated June 26, 1984 passed by the Upazilla Revenue officer. Laxmipur in Miscellaneous Case No. 76 of 1975-76 was illegal, void and in-operative and also for declarations, inter alia, that the "ka" schedule land of the plaint comprising an area of 2.52 acres appertaining to D.S. Khatian No. 334 of Mouja Bijoynagar, P.S. Laximipur orginally belonged to one Shiv Chandra Majumder on the basis of purchase by a registered kabala dated January 19, 1920. By way of amicable partition with other co-sharers Shiv Chandra Majumder used to own and possess 1.76 acres of land, while Raj Kumar Bhowmick used to own and possess the remaining, 76 acre of land. After the death of Raj Kumar Bhowmick his son Chandra Bhushan Bhowmick slold the same jointly to Ayub Ali, respondent No. 1 and Hafer Muhammad Abdul Haque, the appellant. Shiv Chndra Majumder died leaving .2 sons Rajani Kumar Maujumder and Gopal Chandra Majumder who inherited 1.76 acres of land from their father. The two brothers Rajani Kumar Majumder and Gopal Chandra Majumder orally sold their 1.76 acres of land to respondent Nos. I and 2 and parted with possession thereof on receipt of Tk. '6,000/- on 15th Chitra, 1354 B.S. corresponding to March 30, 1948. Thereafter the plaintiff-transferees raised residential structures in a portion of that land continued in possession. Rajani Kumar Majumder and Copal Chandra Majumder filed an application under section 2 of the East Pakistan Disturbed persons (Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 1964 (E.P. Ordinance No. 1 of 1964) against the respondents making certain false allegation and praying for restoration of possession of 1.76 acres  of land which was registered.' as. Misc, Case No. 61 1964 in the Court of Magistrate, First Class, Noakhali, Thereafter on June 17, 1'965 both the parties filed a petition of compromise where in the Parties admitted the Possession  of the respondents in the suit land. The compromise petition was disposed of on July 21,, 1965 but since there were, certain clerical mistakes an application for correction was filed on October 22, '1965 which was allowed by the learned Magistrate. Thereafter the respondents filed Mutation Case No. 76/1975-76 in the Office Of the Revenue Circle Officer, Laximpur and Upazilla Revenue Officer by his order dated May 10, 1984 allowed the Mutation case and directed to open a new Khatian in the names of the respondents with a direction to the Tahsilder to realise rent from them: Thereafter the appellant filed an objection before the Upazilla Revenue officer, Laxmipur praying for Cancellation of the order dated May 10. 1984 by the Upazilla Reveruie Officer and following the objection raised by the appellant, the Upazilla Revenue Officer by his order dated June 26, 1984 cancelled his earlier order. The respondents also claimed that they have acquired title to the suit land by their continuous adverse possession against the real owners and the appellant for more than .12 years, since Rajani Kumar Majumder and Gopal Chandra Majumder admitted possession of the respondents in their compromise petition dated . February 17, 1965 filed in Miscellaneous Case No. 61, of 1964 and they left for India for good in the year 1965. Hence the suit praying for cancellation of the order dated June 26. 1984 passed by the Upazilla Revenue Officer, Laxmipur in Miscellaneous Case No, 76 of 1975-76 and also for  declaration of their title and possession to the suit land. 

 3. The appellant contested the suit by filling a written statement contending, inter alia, that Rajani Kumar Majumder and Gopal Chandra Majumder sold the suit land to him on 19th Chaitra, 1354 13.S. Corresponding to April 3, 1948 at a  consideration of Tk. 3500/- and Rajani Kumar Majumder and Sarada Kumar Bhowmick maternal uncle of minor Copal Chandra Majumder on behalf of the minor executed a Swaianpaira (Memorandum) in his favour and parted with possession of the suit land and since his parchase he has been Possessing the suit land, within the knowledge of all including the respondents by raising residential structures: and he acquired title therein by adverse possession. He further alleged that till 1392 B. S. he paid rents to the Government as marfatder in the names of the original Hindu owners vide rent receipts Ext. "Kha" series and that the respondents have no possession in the suit land. As he was away from the locality in connection with his education in Maktab, on behalf of the Rajani Kumar Majumder and Gopal Chandra Majumder as applicants Misc. Case No. 61 of 1964 was filed in the Court of Magistrate, First Class, Noakhali for restoration of possession of the suit land. In this Miscellaneous case the respondents and the applicants, above named, filed a petition of compromise wherein the respondents admitted possession of the applicants. The respondents then filed an application denying possession of the applicants and prayed for amendment of the petition for compromise which was allowed, After, returning back to his house the appellant filed an objection against the amendment of the petition of compromise which was allowed by the learned Magistrate and thereby rejected the prayer for amendment of the petition of compromise. His further case was that by practicing fraud upon the Upazilla Revenue Officer, Laxmipur the respondents succeeded in getting an order for opening a new Khatian in their names in respect of 1.76 acres of land in Mutation Case No. 76 of 1976-76 but on his objection the Upazilla Revenue Officer cancelled his earlier order.
